findings.title: W4's drift net misindexes on paused demos — motion-strip falsely refuses VALID post-pause strips (reproduced: exit 2)
findings.detail: Strip appends one hash per STEPPED tick; the blessed manifest (run_demo) appends per WALL window — paused windows included. After any pause, prefix comparison shifts → false STATE DIVERGENCE at the first post-pause tick. Over-strict only: no false-green; a re-bless reproduces the identical manifest (goldens cannot be corrupted by this). Frames are also exported before the check refuses (orphan PNGs), and the PR body's 'verified' overstates.
findings.recommended_fix: Index-align: append the paused-window stable-state hash in the strip (mirror run_demo's convention), or track the wall-window index per stepped tick and compare manifest[wall_tick-1]. Verify with `motion-strip pause 71000 72000 100` (want exit 0) + a corrupted-manifest negative.

findings.title: [still present since r3] The delivery-snap pin is still non-decisive — deleting the delivered guard breaks NO test (Perkins mutation-proven)
findings.detail: The production guard is real and verified, but the test's entry anchors still mismatch (entry on_edge=true vs p.on_edge=false), so the guard never decides. Mutation test: guard deleted → 33/33 render tests pass. The PR-body claim 'the pin tests the predicate' is falsified.
findings.recommended_fix: Make the anchor continuous (entry_heading == p.at_node, matching on_edge) with delivered=true → assert snap; companion same-shape delivered=false → assert continuous. Two-line change; the guard then has a decisive pin.

findings.title: Trail-ring drop-oldest shift branch never executes in any test — yet the PR body and test header list it as pinned
findings.detail: The fill test drives 4 snapshots = exactly 3 pushes = full ring; the overflow `else` (shift loop) never runs. An off-by-one in the shift ships silently; the delivered-claims list overstates coverage.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a 5th move in trail_ring_order_and_fill; assert trail[0] advanced to the frac-0.7 frame and trail_n stays 3.

findings.title: trail_ring_stationary_no_push pins a stationary push while asserting the opposite — the non-empty-ring stationary case is never exercised
findings.detail: First call is a snap (early return, no push); the second, STATIONARY call pushes via the empty-ring bootstrap (`moved := echo_n == 0`). trail_n==1 therefore pins a stationary push while the message says it doesn't. The real invariant (stationary frame with a non-empty ring must not push) is untested.
findings.recommended_fix: Seed with two distinct moving frames (ring ≥1), then assert a stationary frame leaves trail_n unchanged; keep the empty-ring bootstrap as its own named assertion.

findings.title: Echo draw application has no assertion anywhere — the fades pin re-derives the ladder math, not the draw code
findings.detail: Goldens render alpha=1.0 (trails_active false) and motion-pixel's exact-color scan excludes blended echoes by construction. The draw-side fade indexing/order is a mutation-surviving hole (P2 residue per the gate).
findings.recommended_fix: One rlsw assertion: a mid-glide frame's echo pixels at the two expected fade strengths (or fold into motion-pixel with a blended-color tolerance).

findings.title: [carried half of r3 N11] measure_packet_motion.py still exits 0 when zero frames track in both strips
